rationale: This is a narrower re-cut of the already-tested Working-Capital-Release-Adjusted Cash Yield, and it is internally inconsistent because lct includes debt in current liabilities and notes payable whose increases never enter oancf, so the haircut penalizes financing inflows that were never counted in the numerator.

The denominator adds a one-year liability *flow* to a market-cap *stock*, a dimensional mismatch that makes the adjustment negligible for most firms so the signal collapses into a plain change-in-earnings-to-price measure — essentially the already-tested Retained Profit Accumulation Yield template and a well-known earnings-growth-to-price anomaly.

The one-sided stock-based deficit penalty is economically distinct from the earlier flow-burn and multiplicative-profitability versions of cash-to-price, and the sign logic is coherent, though it reuses the archive's che/(mktcap + max(penalty,0)) template closely enough that incremental information over Earned-Cash Discount is uncertain.

TREND(cogs/sale) is mechanically the negative of the gross-margin trend, so this is the sign-flipped mirror of the archive's sales-yield × margin-quality family (Durable Margin, Through-Cycle Margin Floor) and adds little beyond a known gross-margin-trend value interaction.

This is a pure parameter/aggregation tweak of Maintenance Cash Runway Discount (MA over 2 → TS_SUM over 3 of the identical oancf−dp burn), i.e., a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Sign logic is internally consistent and the deteriorating-turnover trap leg is economically distinct from the failed leverage-change leg of Rising-Claims Asset Trap, though it reuses that same at/mktcap × trend template and the choice of current assets rather than total assets as the turnover base is unmotivated.
